audit_findings.title: Non-cash pension income may be capitalized as owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $190 million pre-tax in 2025, equal to 39.1% of the $485.5 million anchor; $106 million for the first half of 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Potentially inflates historical OE and the trend-derived anchor by retaining expected pension-asset returns and other non-operating retirement income without assigning the restricted pension assets to equity.
audit_findings.evidence: The non-operating retirement benefit in 2025 was $190 million, compared to $179 million in 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: The pension income is demonstrated, but its inclusion in OE is not. Because the 2025 amount is nearly two-fifths of anchor OE and recurring pension income also appears in 2026, inconsistent treatment is reasonably capable of materially changing the anchor and all scenario values.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile FAS expense, CAS recovery, contributions, and non-operating retirement income for every OE year; remove non-distributable income, apply taxes consistently, and rerun the anchor and scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Unfunded postretirement benefits may be an omitted senior claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $319 million unfunded obligation, equal to 4.7% of base equity value and 65.7% of anchor OE; expected 2026 cash contributions of $35 million, equal to 7.2% of anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: Could reduce OE through benefit payments or reduce the equity bridge as a senior claim, subject to offsets for expense already recognized and CAS recoveries.
audit_findings.evidence: For the year ending December 31, 2026, the Company expects its cash contributions to its other postretirement benefit plans to be approximately $ 35 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The obligation and expected cash payment are demonstrated, but an omission is not: the record does not reconcile accounting expense, cash payments, and CAS recovery. The gross liability is modest relative to base equity value, while recurring net cash runoff could be more significant; the net economic burden remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile postretirement expense, payments, and CAS recoveries by year, then either deduct the net cash runoff in OE or subtract the unfunded economic claim without double counting.

audit_findings.title: Unreserved welding remediation exposure could sit ahead of equity
audit_findings.mechanism: Any unrecovered rework, repayment, penalty, or contract-margin reduction would lower OE or enter the equity bridge as a liability.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company continues to work with its U.S. Navy customer to evaluate the full extent of the matter and cannot at this time predict or reasonably estimate the ultimate outcome of this matter.
audit_findings.explanation: The welding noncompliance and continuing government evaluation are demonstrated, but no loss amount or probability is estimable. The June 2026 filing repeats that the outcome cannot be predicted or reasonably estimated, so this is an existing unresolved exposure rather than merely a forward-looking risk; the record cannot establish materiality.
audit_findings.action: Obtain vessel-level scope, remediation estimates, customer recovery and indemnification terms, insurance coverage, accrued amounts, and subsequent contract-margin adjustments; rerun OE or the bridge if a measurable net exposure emerges.

audit_findings.title: Projected growth may require more capital than the historical OE anchor captures
audit_findings.magnitude: 2026 guidance implies maintenance capital of 1.0%-1.5% and discretionary capital of 3.0%-3.5% of revenue; applied to filed 2025 revenue of $12.484 billion, total capital is $499-$624 million, or $97-$222 million above 2025 capital-expenditure additions of $402 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Growth-producing capacity capital must reduce forecast OE if the modeled 3%-5% growth depends on that investment.
audit_findings.evidence: Our capital expenditures are expected to increase due to investments to expand our shipbuilding capacity.
audit_findings.explanation: The higher capital-spending requirement is demonstrated, but its necessity for each scenario and its treatment in forecast OE are not. The computed increase equals roughly 20%-46% of anchor OE, making inconsistent growth and reinvestment assumptions reasonably capable of materially changing scenario values.
audit_findings.action: Separate maintenance from capacity capital, map required spending to each growth scenario, deduct all growth-enabling capital from forecast OE, and rerun the scenarios without crediting growth from excluded investment.

audit_findings.title: Unrealized investment gains may remain in the earnings numerator
audit_findings.magnitude: filed marketable-security gains of $34 million in 2025, $22 million in 2024, and $23 million in 2023; the 2025 amount equals 7.0% of anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: Potentially inflates historical OE and the trend anchor by capitalizing non-operating investment returns while excluding the related assets from the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The increase in other, net income was primarily driven by an increase in unrealized gains on investments.
audit_findings.explanation: The gains and their inclusion in GAAP earnings are demonstrated, but their retention in calculated OE is not. Their recurring three-year presence could affect the trend and terminal value, yet the record lacks the annual OE reconciliation needed to establish the actual valuation effect.
audit_findings.action: Trace realized and unrealized investment returns through every OE year, remove any retained non-operating gains or pair them with the related net assets and liabilities, then recompute the trend anchor and scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The fully diluted share count is not a true maximum ceiling
audit_findings.magnitude: up to 390,710 additional shares using the exact 2025 target RPSR count, equal to 0.98% of the 39.925598 million valuation denominator; conservatively, base value would decline about $1.66 per share and bull value about $1.85 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Above-target RPSR vesting increases the per-share denominator without changing aggregate equity value.
audit_findings.evidence: All of the RPSRs are subject to the achievement of performance-based targets at the end of the respective vesting periods and will ultimately vest between 0 % and 200 % of grant date value.
audit_findings.explanation: The 200% vesting feature demonstrates that the reported denominator is not a maximum. Even conservatively applying the entire exact year-end target RPSR count as incremental dilution reduces per-share values by less than 1%, far too little to alter the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the exact current RPSR and RSR split, include subsequent grants and forfeitures, and report a 200% RPSR sensitivity while retaining stock-compensation expense.
